tasks.task: Look up the most recent papers related to 'cs.CL', select one and show its abstract.
tasks.answer: Selected paper from the most recent cs.CL listings: 'Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14483). Abstract: Mechanistic interpretability (MI) seeks mechanistic explanations for model behaviors, yet it lacks a formal framework for connecting mechanistic findings to behavioral claims. We propose that MI needs a logic of inference to bridge mechanistic facts and behavioral conclusions, and we introduce the Interpretability Calculus (IC) as a candidate formal system. IC uses syntax for causal interventions and feature quantification, and proof rules for deriving behavioral claims from mechanistic evidence. We demonstrate IC by formalizing a circuit analysis of induction heads, showing how mechanistic findings support a behavioral claim about next-token prediction. We argue that a logic of inference can help MI mature from descriptive case studies into a discipline capable of cumulative, auditable knowledge.

tasks.task: Locate the most recent research paper about 'Algebraic Topology' under Mathematics published on ArXiv. Provide the title of the paper, the name of the authors, and the abstract.
tasks.answer: Most recent Algebraic Topology paper on ArXiv (arXiv:2611.14105, newest announcement date group Wed, 11 Nov 2026): Title: Thom Morphisms, Self-Intersection, and the Sectional Category of a Section. Authors: Paul-Eugène Parent. Abstract: For sections between simply connected spaces of finite rational type, we compare module sectional category, sectional category and relative category after rationalization. Fibre Poincaré duality turns the compatibility of derived evaluation with the section into a derived self-intersection formula. We prove equality of the three invariants under any of four hypotheses: a base-dimension bound, finite total rational homotopy of the fibre, a smooth section with closed manifold fibre, or a compatible relative Frobenius model. Projective bundles over CP^k with fibre CP^r have common value k + r, which is unbounded even for fixed fibre. Whether fibre Poincaré duality alone suffices remains open.

tasks.answer: Latest paper in arXiv Nonlinear Sciences - Chaotic Dynamics (nlin.CD): arXiv:2611.13474 - 'Unified Ott--Antonsen Framework for Stability and Bifurcations in Ring Swarmalators'. Abstract summary: The paper presents a unified theoretical framework based on the generalized Ott--Antonsen manifold for analyzing the stability and bifurcations of collective states in one-dimensional ring swarmalators (models coupling temporal rhythms with spatial swarming). It systematically analyzes four representative collective states -- desynchronization, phase-wave, synchronization, and mixed states -- derives stability conditions and bifurcation boundaries in a two-parameter coupling plane, and validates the theoretical predictions with large-scale numerical simulations, clarifying state selection and nonequilibrium phase transitions in active-matter systems. tasks.task: Query ArXiv for the latest research article in the category of Systems and Control under Computer Science. Summarize the main objective or hypothesis presented in the paper and provide the names of the authors.
tasks.answer: The latest research article in the Systems and Control (cs.SY) category under Computer Science on arXiv is 'Proportional Neuro-Impulsive Control of SISO LTI Systems' (arXiv:2611.13043). Authors: Christian Fernandez Lorden, Elena Petri, W.P.M.H. Heemels, Alessio Franci. Main objective/hypothesis: The paper proposes a neuro-impulsive controller at the crossroads of neuromorphic (spike-based) and impulsive control, consisting of a single integrate-and-fire-like neuron that generates a control input proportional to the system output when the neuron variable reaches a threshold. Its central claim is that any static output-feedback stabilizable single-input single-output (SISO) linear time-invariant (LTI) plant can be made semi-globally asymptotically stable (sGAS) in closed loop with this neuro-impulsive controller, improving on existing fixed-amplitude neuromorphic controllers that only achieve practical stability (at the price of graded spiking inputs). It also provides an algorithm for choosing the controller parameters for a given set of admissible initial conditions, illustrated on an inverted pendulum linearized around its upright equilibrium.

tasks.task: Search for the most recent paper related to non-commutative geometry submitted by an author with the first name John. Provide the title and the abstract.
tasks.answer:
Most recent paper related to non-commutative geometry submitted by an author with the first name John (arXiv advanced search: All fields "non-commutative geometry" AND Author(s) John*, ordered by Announcement date newest first): arXiv:1908.06796

Title: Finite spectral triples for the fuzzy torus

Abstract: We classify all finite spectral triples for the fuzzy torus algebra. We show that each such triple has a direct sum decomposition into standard components, and that the Dirac operator can be written as a sum of twisted partial derivatives. We also discuss the relationship between these finite spectral triples and the spectral triples for the non-commutative torus, showing that the fuzzy torus spectral triples arise as finite-dimensional approximations of the non-commutative torus spectral triples in a precise sense related to non-commutative geometry.
